 BMKG Forecasts Rainy Season to Retreat 20-30 Days, Beware of Accumulating Rainfall 
 26 Oktober 2026, 18:15 | Editorial Team 
 Teddy Kurniawan 
 Reporter 
 Edy Suherli 
 Editor 
 Head of BMKG Teuku Faisal Fathani. (Teddy VOI) 
 Share:
 JAKARTA - The Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) predicts that the rainy season in Indonesia will be delayed by around 20-30 days due to the influence of El Nino. Although the amount of rainfall is predicted to be normal, rain has the potential to accumulate in a shorter time.
 Head of BMKG Teuku Faisal Fathani said that this condition needs to be watched out for because it can increase the potential for wet hydrometeorological disasters at the end of 2026 to early 2027.
 "The average rainy season in Indonesia is expected to be about two to three days, or 20-30 days, due to the influence of El Nino. The rainy season will also accumulate quite a lot in a shorter duration, with normal rain characteristics," said Faisal at the Presidential Palace Complex, Jakarta, Monday, October 26.
 A dasarian is a period of 10 days. Thus, a delay of two to three dasarians means a shift in the onset of the rainy season by about 20-30 days.
 According to Faisal, some parts of Indonesia are expected to enter the rainy season in November to December 2026.
 Meanwhile, the peak of the rainy season is predicted to take place in December 2026 to February 2027.
 "The peak will be in December, January, and February. This is what we need to be aware of because the nature of the rain is normal," he said.
 Faisal explained that the normal rain category refers to the average rainfall based on climatological data over the past 30 years.
 This means that the amount of rain that falls is expected to be relatively the same as normal conditions. However, the time it takes for the rain to fall is shorter.
 "The amount of rain that falls is relatively the same, but the duration is shorter. For the end of this year to early next year, we need to be aware of wet hydrometeorological disasters together," he said.
 Wet hydrometeorological disasters are disasters related to weather and water conditions, such as floods and landslides.
 Faisal conveyed the forecast before attending a limited meeting with the President at the Presidential Palace.
 He said the BMKG had prepared a number of materials to be discussed with the President, including the development of forest and land fires and preparations for dealing with hydrometeorological disasters.
 "I think there will be a lot of things discussed. We have also prepared a lot of materials, ranging from the development of karhutla and how to handle it in the future, then preparing for hydrometeorological disasters," he said.
